verdicts.question: After MeitY's January 2026 consultations, were the DPDP Rules 2025 deadlines (about 13 May 2027 for core duties) shortened for any class of company, and what applies to a small startup handling phone numbers and photos?
verdicts.problems: Verification limits first: this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) and every outbound fetch returned no connection, so no cited page or snippet could be opened today. What I could do was cross-check against the independent v1 pass on the same question (docs/plan/research/handoff/answers-v1/data-it-rules.research.json, 29 Sep 2026), which used a different source set (egazette PDFs for G.S.R. 843(E)/846(E), Financial Express, Hindustan Times, BusinessLine, Rediff, Fortune India, LiveLaw) and reached the same headline: nothing shortened, no startup exemption, core duties about 13 May 2027, Board unstaffed. So the conclusion is corroborated but 'not confirmed by snippet'. Specific issues: (1) Rule 7 is mis-stated in a way that matters for the runbook. The answer says 'tell the Board within 72 hours'; the v1 pass (from the gazette text) has it as intimate the Board WITHOUT DELAY, then furnish the detailed report within 72 hours. A runbook that waits up to 72 hours for first notice would breach the rule; the decision text ('72-hour breach runbook') should read 'immediate intimation to users and the Board, detailed report within 72 hours'. (2) A newer, stronger source was missed: on 14 Aug 2026 MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan told about 30 startups there would be no extension and the notified timelines hold (Fortune India, 14 Aug 2026), and a LiveLaw analysis of 10 Sep 2026 still treats May 2027 as the date and the Board as vacant; both support the answer and should be cited in place of the third-party trackers (dpdprules.org, dcomply) which are not official. (3) 'The MeitY Secretary said on 11 March 2026 that no decision would be taken' is not confirmed; the v1 pass attributes the 'no final decision, startups and MSMEs will not feel it' statement to MeitY's Deepak Goel on 12 Feb 2026, so the date, speaker and source (APAC News Network) need checking. (4) 'None appointed as of 1 Aug 2026' for the Board is stale by two months; the 10 Sep 2026 LiveLaw piece extends it to September but nothing later was checkable. (5) Arithmetic checks out: 13 Nov 2025 + 12 months = 13 Nov 2026; + 18 months = 13 May 2027; PIB's 14 May counts from publication. Penalty caps (250/200/50 crore), Rule 14's 90-day limit, under-18 parental consent and the Third Schedule thresholds (2 crore e-commerce, 50 lakh gaming, 2 crore social media) match the v1 reading of the gazette but no snippet confirmed them today. (6) Refined material chain: the answer only lists households, kabadiwalas and KYC. The 30 Sep 2026 model adds pre-processors, compounders, DWCCs/MRFs, brands with EPR duties, authorised waste handlers and TSDFs, plus processing records (main output, by-products, residual lots, yields) and five price levels. Most of that is business data, but the notice and purpose list must also cover: proprietors' names, phones, PAN/GSTIN and KSPCB consent numbers captured for sole-trader yards and pre-processors (personal data when the business is an individual); Saathi identity and geolocation at pickup and sorting, and any sharing of Saathi records with the Karnataka gig-worker welfare board (a separate legal basis to state in the notice); weighbridge and lot photos that may show workers' faces; L1 household price records tied to phone numbers; and chat between roles. The 400 industrial by-product rows and KSPCB category codes are not personal data and need no consent. Add these to the Rule 3 notice and the Rule 6 access-control matrix before 13 Oct 2026.

verdicts.question: Have amendments to the IT (Intermediary) Rules in 2025-26 changed the 36-hour takedown or the 24-hour/15-day grievance timelines? Which Indian accessibility rules (RPwD Act 2016, IS 17802, GIGW 3.0) apply to a private platform?
verdicts.problems: Same verification limit: no search or fetch was possible this session, so no snippet confirmed any figure; the cross-check is the independent v1 pass (answers-v1, 29 Sep 2026) which used different sources (eGazette, ANI, MediaNama, The Hindu, Financial Express, News18, Hindustan Times, the DEPwD gazette PDF for S.O. 3962(E), guidelines.india.gov.in). The core timeline claims are corroborated by that pass: G.S.R. 775(E) of 22 Oct 2025 (in force 15 Nov 2025) kept 36 hours but restricted who may order; G.S.R. 120(E) of 10 Feb 2026 (in force 20 Feb 2026) cut court/government orders to 3 hours, nudity/impersonation removals to 2 hours, prohibited-content complaints to 36 hours; RPwD s.46 and s.89; Rule 15(1)(c) naming IS 17802 Parts 1 and 2; Rajive Raturi 8 Nov 2024; draft RPwD (Amendment) Rules 2026 S.O. 3962(E) with 12-month/18-month tracks and an ACR. Three things do not hold or are unsupported: (1) 'IS 17802 is freely downloadable' is contradicted by the v1 pass, which states the text must be bought from BIS; the only 'free copy' cited is an archive.org upload of uncertain provenance, not BIS. Founders should budget for the BIS purchase or use BIS's read-only viewer, and treat the WCAG 2.1 AA alignment as an inference (v1 flags it as inferred from the EN 301 549 clause structure), not a confirmed statement. (2) 'Grievance disposal 15 days to 7 days' rests on one law-firm timeline and MediaNama's rule-by-rule report; the v1 pass explicitly asked counsel to verify the 7-day figure against G.S.R. 120(E) itself, and no snippet confirmed it today. Keep the 7-day SLA as the safe design target but mark the figure as needs-counsel. (3) A newer development was missed: Hindustan Times reported on 22 Aug 2026 that MeitY was 'set to notify a portion of the IT Rules for stricter compliances' (the 30 March 2026 draft Second Amendment). The answer says the draft 'had not been notified in any coverage we opened through September 2026' without citing that report; whether part of it was gazetted in September 2026 could not be checked and is an open item, so the status should be partly/needs-counsel on that point. Smaller points: the 2023 RPwD amendment is dated 11 May 2023 here and 10 May 2023 in v1 (SCC blog is 12 May 2023); s.89 is 'up to' Rs 10,000 for a first contravention, not a flat Rs 10,000; the CCPD enforcement figures (155 establishments fined in Feb 2025, 96 in June 2025, audit order 30 Jul 2024) come from a single AZB & Partners note and are not confirmed by any snippet; 'comments closed about 19 Aug 2026' is arithmetically consistent with gazette publication on 20 Jul 2026 plus 30 days. The 180-day retention duties (removed content; registration data after cancellation) match Rule 3(1)(g)-(h) as read by the v1 pass. Refined material chain: the intermediary analysis should extend beyond household-kabadiwala listings and chat to every user-posted item in the new model - pre-processor and compounder processing records with lot photos, by-product and residual-waste listings, the candidate industrial by-product listings (bagasse, fly ash, slag etc.) posted by units against KSPCB category codes, uploaded EPR certificates and consent documents - all of which are third-party content for Rule 3 purposes and need the same report, takedown and 180-day retention paths; and the accessibility target must cover the desktop-style dashboards for yards, pre-processors, recyclers and compounders (S0-S9 state views, yield tables, L1-L5 price screens), not only the phone-first household and Saathi screens. Where the IT Rules (24 h / 7 d), the E-Commerce Rules (48 h / 1 month) and Karnataka gig-worker rules overlap, run the strictest clock.
verdicts.correction: Timelines: yes, changed twice. G.S.R. 775(E) (22 Oct 2025, in force 15 Nov 2025) kept the 36-hour clock in Rule 3(1)(d) but limited takedown intimations to Joint Secretary rank (or DIG for police), reasoned, with legal basis and exact URL, reviewed monthly. G.S.R. 120(E) (10 Feb 2026, in force 20 Feb 2026) cut court or government orders from 36 hours to 3 hours, nudity/sexual/impersonation content from 24 hours to 2 hours, and complaints to remove prohibited content from 72 to 36 hours; it also added AI-content labelling duties. The general grievance clock is reported as cut from 15 to 7 days with the 24-hour acknowledgement unchanged, but that figure is reported by news and law-firm summaries and should be read off G.S.R. 120(E) by counsel before it goes into the legal pages. A 30 March 2026 draft Second Amendment (MeitY advisories binding, MIB oversight, longer retention) proposes no new clocks; Hindustan Times reported on 22 Aug 2026 that MeitY was set to notify part of it, so whether any portion was gazetted in September 2026 is an open item to check on egazette.gov.in and meity.gov.in before 13 Oct 2026. Luma is very likely an intermediary for all user-posted content: listings, photos, chat, processing records and lot photos from pre-processors and compounders, by-product and residual listings, industrial by-product candidate listings, uploaded EPR and KSPCB documents. Rule 3 applies in full: published terms with the prohibited-content categories, a named Grievance Officer with contact details, acknowledge in 24 hours and close in 7 days, 36-hour and 2-hour removal paths, a 3-hour path for official orders, removed content and registration data kept 180 days. Accessibility: the RPwD Act 2016 binds private service providers (s.46) with s.89 fines of up to Rs 10,000 for a first contravention and Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh thereafter; Rule 15(1)(c) of the RPwD Rules 2017 (amended May 2023) names IS 17802 Parts 1 (2021) and 2 (2022) as the ICT standard; the Supreme Court in Rajive Raturi (8 Nov 2024) held Rule 15(1) ultra vires for being only recommendatory; the draft RPwD (Amendment) Rules 2026 (S.O. 3962(E), 16 Jul 2026, gazetted 20 Jul 2026, comments to about 19 Aug 2026) would make IS 17802 mandatory for every establishment offering websites or apps in India, 12 months for turnover of Rs 500 crore or more, 18 months for smaller ones, full conformance in two years, with a published Accessibility Conformance Report; DEPwD was reported (Medianama, 23 Sep 2026) to be targeting notification around January 2027, when the Supreme Court next hears the matter. GIGW 3.0 covers government sites and apps only and is a free checklist for Luma, not a duty. IS 17802 is a BIS standard that must be bought from BIS (or read in BIS's viewer); the archive.org copy is unofficial. Its web clauses are understood to track WCAG 2.1 AA, so build every screen, including the yard, pre-processor, recycler and compounder dashboards, to WCAG 2.1 AA and keep an ACR-style record; confirm the mapping against the purchased standard. Status: partly. Ask a technology lawyer (30 minutes) to confirm intermediary status for the full content set, read the 7-day figure and any September 2026 partial notification off the gazette, and confirm the IS 17802 to WCAG mapping.
